quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation, you must show:

options.text: Only your insurance and registration.
Only your license.
Your license, insurance, and registration.

questions.explanation: You must carry and show your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You need all three documents whenever you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves ahead.

questions.question: A truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus does.
Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through if the intersection is clear and it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through if the intersection is clear and it is safe.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can proceed. First yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection. Only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection.
Lane change.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and prepare to yield or stop before turning.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.explanation: Use low beams in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off the water or fog and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What word appears on a red octagon-shaped sign?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.explanation: An octagon (eight-sided) sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
All the time.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must always have the right of way.

questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that makes you take evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your focus away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. They can cause crashes, injuries, and death.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Slow down and pass carefully.

questions.explanation: When you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and harder to see. Watch for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. They may ride onto the road without warning.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses before going.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let pedestrians in the intersection pass first. Wait until they have fully crossed before you drive.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a car with airbags?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags can hurt children. Anyone age 12 or under must sit in the back seat of a car with airbags.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: Speed up a little.
It is not safe to pass.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other cars in that area. The road ahead has poor visibility, making it unsafe to pass.

questions.question: When you see someone with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until they are far away from your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are far away from your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop for pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog. Always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Also adjust your seat, fasten your seatbelt, and secure items. Do not adjust mirrors while moving.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
To get other drivers moving in traffic.
When you're angry with another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to get other drivers' attention and prevent crashes. Other drivers may not see you unless you alert them.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Speed up.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to turn safely.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane and there is no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at intersections, even if there is no marked crosswalk. Pedestrians have the right-of-way.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden and improper lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.
They drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden and improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers on the road. If you see someone making sudden or improper lane changes, they may be an aggressive driver. Do not challenge them. The safest action is to stay away from them.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, the only way to reduce alcohol's effects is by:

options.text: Taking a cold shower.
Waiting several hours.
Drinking several cups of coffee.

questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers will not help. Your body needs about one hour to remove the effects of one drink.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Focus on your driving and do not take other drivers' actions personally. Plan extra time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio volume.
Park in a safe area and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in a safe area and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or need the radio loud to stay awake, you are too tired to drive safely. Find a safe place to park and rest.
